summary.title: GLM-5V-Turbo: Toward a Native Foundation Model for Multimodal Agents

setting_and_object.category: Architecture / System (multimodal foundation model technical report)

details: Agentic foundation models must perceive and act over heterogeneous context (images, video, GUIs, webpages, documents), yet multimodal perception is usually bolted onto a language model as an auxiliary interface.
Adding vision typically comes at the cost of the base model's text coding/agentic ability.

GLM-5V-Turbo, a vision-language foundation model built for native multimodal agency, whose distinctive components are CogViT (a parameter-efficient vision encoder trained via dual-teacher distillation-based masked image modeling followed by NaFlex contrastive image-text pretraining) and Multimodal Multi-Token Prediction (MMTP), which feeds the MTP head a single shared learnable <|image|> token in place of visual embeddings while preserving visual positional information.
Capability is shaped by joint reinforcement learning across 30+ task categories spanning perception, reasoning, and agentic execution, plus a multimodal toolchain and agent-framework integration.
Accompanying contribution: ImageMining, a vision-centric deep-search benchmark requiring agentic on-image tool use ("think and deep search with image").

Stage 1: masked image modeling (35% mask, 224x224) distilling into feature spaces of dual teachers, SigLIP2 (semantics) and DINOv3 (texture); data mix 80% high-quality natural images, 10% instruction data, 10% scientific imagery; Muon optimizer with cosine decay; QK-Norm for stability.

Stage 2: contrastive image-text pretraining with NaFlex variable-resolution inputs, SigLIP sigmoid loss at 64K global batch size with bidirectional distributed implementation, 8B bilingual (Chinese-English) image-text pairs, module-specific LRs for vision/text/projection.

Three options compared for feeding image context to the MTP head: (1) pass LLM-input visual embeddings, (2) mask out all visual tokens (reduces to text-only MTP), (3) replace visual tokens with a shared learnable <|image|> token keeping positions.

Ablation on a 0.5B model compares training loss of Option 1 vs Option 3; system criteria include pipeline-parallel communication of visual embeddings and compatibility with sequence/context parallelism.

Pretraining mixes plain text with multimodal data across world knowledge, interleaved image-text, OCR, coding, GUI, video, multimodal tool use, spatial perception, grounding, and academic problem solving, with emphasis on multimodal coding data.

Joint RL over 30+ task categories, including relative visual policy optimization for UI-to-code, plus on-policy distillation; GUI agents trained over a task hierarchy (element perception, grounding, single-step action, trajectory-level action) in both SFT and RL, with critic data on perception errors.

RL stack: unified VLM RL Gym for single/multi-step tasks, decoupled reward system (local rule verifiers, async model judges), per-request completion callbacks and early-abort with prompt caching, ViT/projector-specific recomputation plus CPU offload, CP/TP partitioning moved into data loading aligned to downsample groups, async all-to-all dispatch, and joint bin-packing over sequence length and ViT token count (~7 GB GPU comm buffer savings from moving Python objects off the GPU path).

217 curated cases from manually collected trace samples across seven domains (Social, Entertainment, Products, Places, Rich Text, Nature, Science) and five reasoning categories (universal recognition, spatio-temporal, event, text-based, visual search).

Automated pipeline for knowledge discovery, QA reconstruction, and filtering, enforcing a WEB_VISUAL "Visual Jump" constraint so intermediate hops require visual transitions rather than textual/parametric shortcuts; plus dedicated OCR-search data for charts, maps, posters.

Four categories: multimodal coding (Design2Code, Flame-VLM-Code, Vision2Web), multimodal tool use (ImageMining, BrowseComp-VL, MMSearch, MMSearch-Plus, SimpleVQA, Facts, V*), GUI agents (OSWorld, AndroidWorld, WebVoyager), and text-only coding/Claw (CC-Bench-V2, PinchBench, ClawEval, ZClawBench).

Comparisons against Claude Opus 4.6, Kimi K-2.5, prior GLM-4.6V, and the language-only base model GLM-5-Turbo; deployment via Claude Code, OpenClaw/AutoClaw, plus 15 official skills and a proprietary zai_* multimodal toolchain.

key_findings.finding: Representing image context in the MTP head by a single shared learnable <|image|> token is better than passing visual embeddings, on both optimization and systems grounds.
key_findings.evidence: A 0.5B-model ablation shows lower training loss and more stable convergence for the <|image|> design versus directly feeding visual embeddings; it also removes the need to propagate visual embeddings across pipeline-parallel stages and stays compatible with sequence/context parallelism, unlike full visual-token masking.

key_findings.finding: Joint multi-task RL over 30+ categories yields broad, simultaneous gains across perception, reasoning, and agentic tasks with little cross-domain interference.
key_findings.evidence: Over SFT, RL improves RefCOCO-avg by 4.8%, PointBench 3.2%, MVBench 5.6%, SUNRGBD 3D grounding 7.7%, OCRBench 4.2%, CharXiv 7.7%, STEM (MMMU/MathVista/LogicVista) 1.8%, OSWorld 4.9%, MMSearch 3.5%, CC-Backend 0.2%; multi-task training also stabilized narrow-domain tasks where single-task RL oscillates, with observed transfer of thinking patterns across domains.

key_findings.finding: Native multimodal agentic capability can be added without eroding the text-only coding ability of the language base model.
key_findings.evidence: GLM-5V-Turbo matches or exceeds its language-only base GLM-5-Turbo on CC-Backend (22.8), CC-Frontend (68.4), and CC-RepoExploration (72.2), while reaching 94.8 on Design2Code (above Claude Opus 4.6) and strong Claw-framework results (PinchBench 87.0/80.7, ClawEval 57.7/75.0, ZClawBench 57.6).

key_findings.finding: Multimodal toolchain expansion produces large jumps on vision-centric deep-search and browsing benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: MMSearch-Plus reaches 30.0, roughly an eightfold improvement over GLM-4.6V; BrowseComp-VL 51.9, ImageMining 30.7, MMSearch 72.9, SimpleVQA 78.2, plus GUI results of 75.7 on AndroidWorld and 62.3 on OSWorld, matching or exceeding Kimi K-2.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 in these categories.
